new.title: Watch the sunset from Van Fortress, ancient Tushpa
new.desc: Van Fortress is a long limestone ridge built by the Urartian king Sarduri I in the 9th century BC. It served as the Urartian capital Tushpa for about 300 years. The Madır (Sardur) Tower by the entrance carries Sarduri's cuneiform inscriptions, and rock tombs and more inscriptions line the cliff.
new.tip: Climb in the late afternoon for the sunset over Lake Van. Old Van lies just south of the rock.
new.q: Van Kalesi, Eski Van Yolu, Buzhane, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Walk the 1567 Hüsrev Paşa complex in Old Van
new.desc: The Hüsrev Paşa complex was built in 1567 and consists of a mosque, tomb, madrasa, han and bath. It is traditionally linked to the architect Sinan. Its tile work was largely lost to Russian damage and later treasure hunters, and the site is still being excavated and restored.
new.tip: Combine it with the Kaya Çelebi Mosque and the fortress, all within a short walk. Wear sturdy shoes because paths are uneven.
new.q: Hüsrev Paşa Camii, Eski Van, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Look inside the Kaya Çelebi Mosque in Old Van
new.desc: Kaya Çelebi Mosque was begun around 1660 by Kaya Çelebizade Koçi Bey and finished by Mehmet Bey after Koçi Bey's execution. It stands near the old city walls and is the only historic building in Old Van still in use.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times and dress modestly. Some sources note the door is often locked, so ask nearby.
new.q: Kaya Çelebi Camii, Eski Van, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: See the Seljuk minarets of the Ulu and Kızıl mosques
new.desc: Of Old Van's Ulu Cami and Kızıl Cami, only the minarets survive. The Ulu Cami minaret is a Seljuk brick tower, and both stand among the ruins south of the fortress.
new.tip: Photograph them in morning light. Beside them are the Çifte Hamam ruins and an Armenian church site.
new.q: Kızıl Camii Minaresi, Eski Van, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Find the roofless Çifte Hamam in Old Van
new.desc: The Çifte Hamam (Hüsrev Paşa Hamamı) is a double bath in the middle of Old Van, south of the Kızıl Minare mosque. Its roof has collapsed and no inscription names its builder, but it is generally linked to the Hüsrev Paşa complex.
new.tip: Best on a longer Old Van walk with the Ottoman marketplace excavations nearby.
new.q: Hüsrev Paşa Hamamı (Çifte Hamam), Eski Van, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Visit the ruined Armenian church of Surp Vartan
new.desc: Surp Vardan (Surp Vartan) is believed to date from around the 15th century and was built at the foot of the sheer cliff of Van Fortress. Nearby lies Surp Stephanos, where only part of a small brick dome remains. The area was home to a large Armenian community before 1915.
new.tip: Reach it on foot from the fortress entrance. Little remains, so read up on Old Van first.
new.q: Surp Vartan Kilisesi, Eski Van, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: See the Urartian gold at Van Museum
new.desc: Van Museum is a modern building that replaced the older museum damaged in the 2011 earthquakes. It holds what Turkish officials call the world's largest Urartian collection, with gold jewellery, bronze belts and plates engraved with lions, bulls and sphinxes.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday, daytime hours, but check current times. Allow about two hours.
new.q: Van Müzesi, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Meet the odd-eyed cats at the Van Cat House
new.desc: The Van Cat Research and Application Centre, known as Van Kedi Villası, sits on the Yüzüncü Yıl University campus. It protects the Van cat breed, famous for its odd-coloured eyes. It receives tens of thousands of visitors a year, and a programme gives out about 100 cats to families.
new.tip: Visits are popular during school holidays. Check the university's current opening times before going.
new.q: Van Kedisi Araştırma ve Uygulama Merkezi, Yüzüncü Yıl Üniversitesi, Zeve Kampüsü, Tuşba, Van

new.title: Taste otlu peynir in the Historic Cheese Bazaar
new.desc: The Tarihi Peynirciler Çarşısı is a restored arasta-style bazaar built in the early Republican era, with 55 shops. It is known for Van's geographically protected herbed cheese, otlu peynir, made with wild herbs. Restoration was done in 2018.
new.tip: Ask to taste before you buy. Prices have risen sharply, so compare shops.
new.q: Tarihi Peynirciler Çarşısı, Bahçıvan, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Swim at Mollakasım, Lake Van's Blue Flag beach
new.desc: Mollakasım Public Beach in Tuşba has held a Blue Flag since 2018 and is described as the only Blue Flag beach on a lake in Türkiye. It has lifeguards and was renovated, with free entry reported.
new.tip: Go in July or August when the water is warmest. Lake Van is soda water, so rinse off afterwards.
new.q: Mollakasım Halk Plajı, Mollakasım Mahallesi, Tuşba, Van

new.title: Hike Mount Erek above Van
new.desc: Erek Dağı is a 3,204 m mountain overlooking Van and Lake Van. Hiking guides list a summit route of about three hours with wide views over the lake and the city.
new.tip: Go from June to September. Start early and carry water, as snow lingers into early summer.

new.title: Eat breakfast at Sütçü Kenan on Kahvaltı Sokağı
new.desc: Sütçü Kenan opened in 1946 and is run by the third generation of the same family on Breakfast Street. It serves a Van spread with otlu peynir. It is open for breakfast only.
new.tip: Arrive before 10 a.m. Order the full serpme and try otlu peynir.
new.q: Sütçü Kenan Kahvaltı Salonu, Kahvaltıcılar Sokağı, Cumhuriyet Caddesi, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Eat zıvırçe at Urartu Han
new.desc: Urartu Han serves zıvırçe, a pan-cooked lavaş with otlu peynir, plus walnut and dried-apple jams, in the Bahçıvan quarter of İpekyolu.
new.tip: Order zıvırçe with the walnut jam.
new.q: Urartu Han Van Kahvaltısı, Meçhul Asker Sokak, Bahçıvan, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Try kavut with honey at Balcı Dede Kahvaltı Evi
new.desc: Balcı Dede Kahvaltı Evi opens at 06:00 and is known for kavut, a roasted-flour porridge, served with honey. The ground floor also sells breakfast groceries.
new.tip: Buy honey and cheese to take home downstairs.
new.q: Balcı Dede Kahvaltı Evi, İskele Caddesi, Alipaşa, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Eat kavurga in Hüsrev Paşa Park near the fortress
new.desc: Şehr-i Van Sofrası is inside Hüsrev Paşa Parkı on the road to Van Castle. It serves kavurga, a crunchy roasted grain eaten by hand.
new.tip: Stop here before or after the fortress.
new.q: Şehr-i Van Sofrası, Eski Kale Yolu, Hüsrev Paşa Parkı, Buzhane, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Taste Van culture at Adem Şef Kültür Sofrası
new.desc: Adem Şef Van'ın Kültür Sofrası on Toraman Sokak has walls hung with paintings of daily life in Van and serves regional dishes.
new.q: Adem Şef Van'ın İlk Kültür Sofrası, Toraman Sokak, İpekyolu Bulvarı, Alipaşa, İpekyolu, Van

new.title: Taste eggplant jam at Edremit Ahtamara Organik
new.desc: Edremit Ahtamara Organik Kahvaltı is on Sahil Caddesi No:318 beside the old municipality building. It serves eggplant jam and opens at 06:00.
new.q: Edremit Ahtamara Organik Kahvaltı, Sahil Caddesi 318, Yeni Cami, Edremit, Van

new.title: Eat Lake Van fish at Altınsu Balık in Edremit
new.desc: Altınsu Balık Restorant in Edremit is rated 4.9 on Restaurant Guru from more than 1,200 ratings and serves local fish dishes. Lake Van's pearl mullet, inci kefali, is endemic and fishing is banned from 15 April to 15 July.
new.tip: Ask whether inci kefali is available in the season.
